clue.text: Beer is a big hit

blocks.note: first meaning: an old British slang word for beer
second meaning: a heavy blow or punch

explanation.surface: A pub boast that some ale has become a best-seller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big hit' reads as commercial success for the beer, but it means a hard thump.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a pint of ale can be called this, and the same word means a forceful punch or blow.

clue.text: Dictator in exile, but might he get out after noon?

definitions.text: Dictator in exile, but might he get out after noon?

blocks.note: surface reading: a deposed tyrant living abroad, as Uganda's ruler did after 1979

blocks.clueFragment: might he get out after noon?
blocks.note: setter's reading: his name splits as the morning abbreviation plus a word for being at home, so after twelve he would be out

explanation.surface: A deposed tyrant in exile wonders whether he could escape his confinement in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the surname as AM IN: in before noon, so once it is PM he would be OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Idi Amin, Uganda's military ruler, fled into exile in 1979 after his brutal regime was overthrown.

clue.text: Wagner's Ring? No - not all hell let loose

definitions.note: possessive standing for a work by Wagner

indicators.note: not all of the word means one letter is left off its end
letters let loose are freed to scatter into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the place of torment with its final letter dropped

explanation.surface: Someone guesses Wagner's Ring cycle and is told no, it is something else from the composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wagner's Ring' looks like one phrase naming the cycle; Wagner's is the definition and Ring is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Lohengrin is a romantic opera by Richard Wagner, first staged in 1850, about the swan knight.

clue.text: Quick pasta sauce keeps the runs in

indicators.note: the sauce keeps something inside it, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: the Genoese basil sauce
R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A speedy pasta sauce that, alas, brings on diarrhoea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The runs' suggests an upset stomach, but here it is cricket's R.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the Italian tempo marking means very fast, and it is used generally for quickly or instantly.

clue.text: Computer designs Viagra by way of missing chips out

indicators.note: the drug name is missing a phrase, so those letters come away from its front
out means disordered or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
via means by way of, and these letters are removed from the drug name
taken as written

explanation.surface: An odd tale of computer chips going missing, with Viagra somehow involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By way of' reads as a link, but it is VIA, taken from the start of Viagra.
explanation.definitionFit: Graphics are the images and visual designs produced or displayed by computers.

clue.text: Atrocious Chilean, go repent!

indicators.note: something atrocious is badly done, so the letters following are mangled into another order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A demand that a cruel Chilean leader go away and repent his crimes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and a fitting description of the man.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusto Pinochet was the army general who seized power in Chile in 1973 and ruled brutally until 1990.

clue.text: What makes lemon fizzy receives the cold fizzy drink award

indicators.note: one piece receives the others, taking them inside itself

blocks.note: add these letters to lemon and you get the fizzy drink lemonade
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a carbonated soft drink

explanation.surface: Talk of lemons and fizzy drinks, as if handing out a prize for the best soda.
explanation.walkthrough: The ending -ADE is what turns lemon into lemonade.
explanation.definitionFit: An accolade is an honour or award given in recognition of merit.

clue.text: See 9
Chaotic drama with corgi and ticker tape

indicators.note: chaotic means thrown into disorder, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A messy scene involving a corgi and a parade with ticker tape.
explanation.walkthrough: Ticker is slang for the heart, so its tape is the paper printout of its beats.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardiogram is the paper trace recording the heart's electrical activity; ticker is slang for heart.

clue.text: Round number

blocks.note: surface reading: a number ending in zero, such as a hundred
setter's reading: how many greens make up a complete round of golf

explanation.walkthrough: A 'round number' sounds like a tidy figure; here it is the count of holes in a golf round.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard round of golf is played over a full course of that many holes.

clue.text: Some elephant in call for salad vegetable

indicators.note: some of the animal's name means only part of it is used, its opening letters
one piece sits in the other

blocks.note: a cry is a call or shout
the first three letters of the animal's name

explanation.surface: An elephant trumpeting for a salad seems to be the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Celery is a crunchy stalk vegetable often eaten raw in salads.

clue.text: True-to-life representation of acts in ritual

indicators.note: a representation re-presents its material in a different form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A realistic portrayal of ceremonial rites, as in an anthropology film.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturalistic art or writing depicts things realistically, as they appear in real life.

clue.text: Corruption of the police right subject for Fergie's children's books?

indicators.note: corruption spoils and distorts, so the letters are put out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Police corruption seems an unlikely theme for a duchess's books for children.
explanation.walkthrough: Fergie is Sarah Ferguson, Duchess of York, who wrote the Budgie the Little Helicopter books.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarah Ferguson's children's stories star Budgie, a small talking rotorcraft, so that aircraft is their subject.

clue.text: Hairy beast's stomach

blocks.note: first meaning: a large furry animal such as a grizzly
second meaning: as a verb, to tolerate or put up with

explanation.surface: The belly of a shaggy animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stomach' reads as a noun after the possessive; it is the verb meaning endure.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the big shaggy mammal and is also a verb meaning endure or tolerate.

clue.text: Digs for diamonds with spirit in the wood

indicators.note: the pieces go in the last one, which surrounds them

blocks.note: logs are cut wood
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone digging for diamonds in a forest, fortified by spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digs' looks like a verb about excavating; it is British slang for rented rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Digs is informal British for rented accommodation, the same as lodgings.

clue.text: Being kind, we'll erect a section for the occupier

indicators.note: only a section of the words is wanted, a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across these three words

explanation.surface: A kindly builder promising to put up a section of building for a tenant.
explanation.definitionFit: An indweller is one who dwells within a place, an inhabitant or occupant.

clue.text: Orc with fleas should be put out, not in the house

indicators.note: putting something out disturbs it, so the letters are arranged differently

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A flea-ridden orc should be shut outdoors, like a mangy dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Al fresco is Italian-derived for in the open air, outdoors rather than indoors.

clue.text: Cabaret actress - literally, little girl in short dress

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other

blocks.note: a miniskirt or minidress
a girl's name, short for Eleanor or Helen

explanation.surface: A cabaret performer is described as a little girl in a skimpy frock.
explanation.walkthrough: Cabaret is the 1972 film; 'literally' notes that the star's name is these pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Liza Minnelli won an Oscar playing Sally Bowles in the 1972 film Cabaret.

clue.text: See 25
Strike a light, council meeting isn't getting held up

indicators.note: the letters are held inside the words before
in a down answer, up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters run across the second and third words

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise that a council meeting is not being delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike a light' looks like the British exclamation of surprise; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike a match or light is to set it burning, which is to kindle or set alight.

clue.text: Mum's the word?

blocks.note: surface reading: the idiom for keeping a secret
setter's reading: the language belonging to one's mum, the first one learned

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom asks for silence, but read literally it is mum's speech.
explanation.definitionFit: One's native language is the one first learned from a parent in early childhood.

clue.text: Being most advanced?

blocks.note: surface reading: asks about being furthest ahead, as in a race
setter's reading: the living creature reckoned the most highly evolved, which goes before being

explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' reads as a verb, but it is the noun completed by the answer in a familiar phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Our species is commonly regarded as the most evolved creature, a person or human being.

clue.text: See 25
Foxes protected by bats

blocks.note: first meaning: baffles or puzzles
second meaning: the wooden posts of a cricket wicket, guarded by the batsman

explanation.surface: Foxes sheltered by flying bats, a night-time woodland scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The bats are cricket bats, not animals; in cricket the batter defends the wicket's three upright posts.
explanation.definitionFit: To stump someone is to baffle them, and the wicket's upright posts are called stumps.

clue.text: That woman keeps single to threaten family values?

indicators.note: the woman keeps something inside her

blocks.note: the female pronoun
I is the Roman numeral for one
to loom is to hang over threateningly

explanation.surface: A woman keeps a single parent's household together against threats to family values.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Family values' sounds like moral principles; it means valuables a family owns.
explanation.definitionFit: An heirloom is a valued possession handed down through generations of a family.

clue.text: Disease carried by sea and road due to spread, calling for plague victims on the street?

definitions.text: calling for plague victims on the street?

indicators.note: one piece is carried inside another
spread means scattered about, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the briny is a name for the sea
a painful disease of the joints
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A disease spreading by sea and road, and a cry in the street for the plague dead.
explanation.walkthrough: The plague surface makes 'Disease' look like the definition; it is GOUT, held inside the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: During plague outbreaks, collectors pushed carts through streets shouting this call for corpses to be brought from houses.

clue.text: Slips when heading off naughty children

indicators.note: the heading, the first letter, is taken off

blocks.note: unruly children are called little terrors

explanation.surface: Kids slipping away when sent off for being naughty.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small mistake, so slips are minor mistakes or blunders.
